The '''Gorgaria system''' was located in the [[Karthakk sector/Legends|Karthakk sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was home to the [[Species/Legends|species]] known as the [[Gorgarian buzzadder]].<ref name="Journal7" /><ref name="Planetnamia" />

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan}}
Around [[3637 BBY]],<ref name="Date SoR">{{TORweb|url=community/showthread.php?p=9852711#edit9852711|text=Charles Boyd on Forums: "Dear Story Team, What Year Are We Currently In?" (1)}} &mdash; According to ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''{{'s}} lead designer, [[Charles Boyd]], the majority of the events of the digital expansion [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan|''Shadow of Revan'']] take place in approximately [[3637 BBY]]. The Crew Skill mission "Synthesis of Ruin" is part of the ''Shadow of Revan'' expansion and therefore also takes place around that [[Standard year/Legends|year]].</ref> [[Scientist/Legends|scientists]] from the Gorgaria [[Star system/Legends|system]] claimed to have synthesized a [[Poison/Legends|poison]] more [[Death/Legends|lethal]] than [[Ziroxin-12/Legends|Ziroxin-12]],<ref name="Synthesis of Ruin">{{TORcite|exp=shadow|type=crewskill|Bioanalysis|Synthesis of Ruin}}</ref> a chemical developed by the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]].<ref name="LSS">{{TORcite|type=space|Llanic Station Strike}}</ref> The future [[Alliance Commander|commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]]<ref name="Commander">{{TORcite|exp=kotfe|chapter=3}} establishes that [[Alliance Commander|the Outlander]]&mdash;who becomes the [[Commander/Legends|commander]] of the future [[Eternal Alliance]] in "Chapter IX: The Alliance"&mdash;also was the player-controlled character in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Shadow of Revan]]''.</ref> subsequently tasked a companion with researching the validity of the scientists' claims.<ref name="Synthesis of Ruin" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
The Gorgaria system was introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', written by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]], which placed it in grid square Q-17.<ref name="TEA" />
